texts.li: {A_nameDef} finally confessed to eating the chocolate {B_nameDef} had been saving since the crash. {B_nameDef} took a long breath and let it go.
{A_nameDef} admitted to {B_nameDef} that the broken mug was not the cat's fault. {B_nameDef} said the cat deserved an apology too.
{A_nameDef} owned up to {B_nameDef} that it was {A_objective}, not the wind, who knocked over {B_nameDef}'s snowman. {B_nameDef} had known for weeks.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} {A_possessive} real name, the one from before. {B_nameDef} promised to forget it, and won't.
Late at night, {A_nameDef} showed {B_nameDef} the old letter sewn into the lining of {A_possessive} coat. Neither of them said much afterwards.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} why {A_pronoun} really left home. It was not the story {A_nameDef} tells at dinner.
{B_nameDef} was dead on {B_possessive} feet, so {A_nameDef} took {B_possessive} night watch and sent {B_objective} to bed.
{A_nameDef} quietly finished {B_nameDef}'s hauling while {B_nameDef} napped behind the granary. Nobody needs to know.
When {B_nameDef} came down with the shakes, {A_nameDef} worked both their shifts and only complained about it a little.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} had a shouting match over three smokeleaf joints owed since last winter. It was never about the smokeleaf.
{B_nameDef} repeated something {A_nameDef} had said in confidence. {A_nameDef} found out at dinner, from someone else.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued about the last raid until one of them said something unforgivable. Neither will say who.
{B_nameDef} spent another evening laughing by the fire with someone else. {A_nameDef} sat across the room, mending a sock that was not torn.
{A_nameDef} has noticed that {B_nameDef} has a new favorite person to eat with. {A_nameDef} has mentioned noticing it several times.
{B_nameDef} went fishing without {A_nameDef}, with someone {A_nameDef} has decided not to like.
{A_nameDef}'s favorite hammer snapped clean in half, and {A_nameDef} has told everyone that {B_nameDef} sawed it. {B_nameDef} has told everyone that {A_nameDef} is unhinged.
{A_nameDef} found {A_possessive} workbench set a hair too low, and is certain {B_nameDef} did it. Nobody else can see the difference.
A whole row of {A_nameDef}'s seedlings died overnight, right where {B_nameDef} was seen walking. {B_nameDef} swears it was only a shortcut.
{A_nameDef} told the table about killing a warg with a frying pan. {B_nameDef} said {B_pronoun} once killed two, with the lid.
{A_nameDef} mentioned walking thirty kilometers on a broken ankle. {B_nameDef} mentioned walking forty, on two.
Every time {A_nameDef} finished a story at dinner, {B_nameDef} had a bigger one. By the end of the meal, both of them had single-handedly fought off the same raid, twice.
{B_nameDef} watched {A_nameDef} patch the wall under fire and, afterwards, gave {A_objective} a single nod. From {B_nameDef}, that is a speech.
{B_nameDef} tasted {A_nameDef}'s stew, paused, and said "not bad". {A_nameDef} has repeated this to everyone.
{B_nameDef} admitted, through clenched teeth, that {A_nameDef}'s work on the new barn was the best in the colony.
At dinner, {A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef}, loudly, whether {B_pronoun} had cooked the stew or just sat in it.
{A_nameDef} raised a toast at dinner "to {B_nameDef}, who has never once been the reason we won a fight". Nobody drank.
{A_nameDef} told the whole table that {B_nameDef} snores like a dying muffalo. {B_nameDef} left without finishing {B_possessive} meal.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} ended up nose to nose over the last seat by the fire. The whole room went quiet.
{B_nameDef} jostled {A_nameDef}'s arm in the mess hall and the soup went everywhere. Fists clenched, and somebody dropped a spoon.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} to say it again. {B_nameDef} said it again.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent the evening sparring with sticks behind the barracks. Both limped to dinner, grinning.
{A_nameDef} showed {B_nameDef} the move that saved {A_possessive} life in the last raid: slowly, then fast, then on {B_nameDef}.
{A_nameDef} woke up shouting, back in the last fight. {B_nameDef} sat with {A_objective} until dawn and never asked a single question.
{B_nameDef} found {A_nameDef} at the perimeter at three in the morning, rifle in hand, staring at nothing. {B_nameDef} stayed and stared too, until the sun came up.
A cut from the last raid reopened on {B_nameDef}'s arm. {A_nameDef} stitched it shut by candlelight, badly, telling terrible jokes the whole time.
{B_nameDef} had been hiding a graze since the fight. {A_nameDef} noticed, swore at {B_objective}, and cleaned it properly.
{B_nameDef} got the same step of {SKILL} wrong all afternoon. Eventually {A_nameDef} put down the tools and went to stare at a wall.
{A_nameDef} tried to explain {SKILL} to {B_nameDef} five different ways, and none of them worked. Both went to bed annoyed.
For the first time, {B_nameDef} did a piece of work in {SKILL} better than {A_nameDef} could have. {A_nameDef} said so out loud, then went off to practice.
{A_nameDef} checked {B_nameDef}'s {SKILL} work for mistakes and found none. {A_nameDef} checked again, and still found none.
{B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} a question about {SKILL} that {A_nameDef} couldn't answer. They worked it out together, and both came away knowing more.
{B_nameDef} tried a {SKILL} trick nobody had shown {B_objective}. {A_nameDef} watched, frowned, and quietly started doing it too.
{B_nameDef}'s lesson in {SKILL} ended with a small fire, a smaller explosion, and {A_nameDef} missing an eyebrow.
Halfway through the {SKILL} lesson, {B_nameDef} did exactly what {A_nameDef} had said not to do. The cleanup took longer than the lesson.
{A_nameDef} demonstrated some {SKILL} for {B_nameDef} with great confidence, and got it completely wrong. They agreed not to tell anyone.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} barely knew each other until they spent an hour arguing about how to tame a boomalope. Now they can't stop talking about it.
{A_nameDef} caught {B_nameDef} naming the chickens, and {A_nameDef} had names for them already. They compared lists until dark.
{A_nameDef} complimented {B_nameDef}'s new haircut, but {B_nameDef} had not had a haircut. Nobody knows what happens now.
{A_nameDef} waved at {B_nameDef} across the field. {B_nameDef} took it for a rude gesture and has been cold ever since.
{B_nameDef} thought {A_nameDef} was asking {B_objective} out. {A_nameDef} had been asking for the salt.
{A_nameDef} borrowed {B_nameDef}'s good knife without asking and gave it back with a chip in the blade.
{B_nameDef} caught {A_nameDef} wearing {B_possessive} coat and was told it had just been lying there. It had been lying on {B_nameDef}.
{A_nameDef} borrowed {B_nameDef}'s bedroll for a hunting trip. It came back smelling of boomalope.
{A_nameDef} noticed {B_nameDef} eating alone and looking grim, so {A_nameDef} sat down and talked about nothing until {B_nameDef} smiled.
{B_nameDef} found {B_possessive} torn boots mended and waiting by the door. {A_nameDef} claims to know nothing about it.
{A_nameDef} brought {B_nameDef} a cup of something hot in the middle of a bad day, and left before {B_nameDef} could say thanks.
{A_nameDef} studied {B_nameDef}'s sculpture for a long moment and asked whether it was meant to be a tumor.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that {B_possessive} cooking was proof the colony could survive anything.
{A_nameDef} informed {B_nameDef} that {B_pronoun} walks like a wounded boomalope. {A_nameDef} meant it helpfully.
{A_nameDef} watched {B_nameDef} butcher a muffalo and remarked, pleasantly, that people come apart much the same way.
{B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} whether {A_pronoun} missed anyone from before. {A_nameDef} gave it honest thought, said no, and smiled.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} exactly how long a body takes to stop smelling in this climate. {B_nameDef} had not asked.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have invented a secret language. It is mostly clicks, and the word for adults is very rude.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} buried a box of treasures behind the barn: a bolt, a bird skull and one silver coin. The map is hidden in a second, secret place.
{A_nameDef} dared {B_nameDef} to touch the freezer door after dark. {B_nameDef} did it, and they both ran off screaming, delighted.
{A_nameDef} dared {B_nameDef} to sneak up on the sleeping muffalo, and {B_nameDef} got close enough to touch it. They are both legends now, at least to each other.
{A_nameDef} followed {B_nameDef} around all day asking why: why the sky, why the raiders, why the doctor keeps the leg. {B_nameDef} answered every one, mostly honestly.
{A_nameDef} begged {B_nameDef} for a story until {B_nameDef} gave in: two hours about a giant squirrel. {A_nameDef} wants another.
{A_nameDef} insisted on helping {B_nameDef} with the chores, which made them take three times as long. {B_nameDef} let {A_objective} help anyway.
{A_nameDef} has been pacing out {B_nameDef}'s bedroom when nobody is looking. It is, apparently, a full step bigger than {A_nameDef}'s own.
{A_nameDef} complimented {B_nameDef}'s room through gritted teeth, then spent the evening glaring at {A_possessive} own ceiling.
{A_nameDef} described the last raid to {B_nameDef} over dinner, wound by wound, with gestures. {B_nameDef} pushed {B_possessive} bowl away.
{A_nameDef} explained to {B_nameDef} what a shotgun does at close range while {B_nameDef} was eating stew. With sound effects.
{A_nameDef} explained {B_nameDef}'s own job to {B_objective}, slowly, with diagrams. The worst part is that {B_nameDef} learned something.
{A_nameDef} corrected {B_nameDef}'s grammar in the middle of a raid warning. {B_nameDef} is still annoyed, and still alive.
{A_nameDef} invited {B_nameDef} to admire a lovely little fire {A_nameDef} had made. {B_nameDef} would like to know where the bench went.
{A_nameDef} spent dinner telling {B_nameDef} about every fire {A_pronoun} had ever seen, with real warmth. {B_nameDef} has started sleeping near the door.
